title: list_features prints facing "up" and a canonical normal for a face whose outside cannot be told (open or T-junction shell) - the refusal-shaped field #956 asked for never shipped

body:
## What happens

On a model whose shell `pick::align::outward_normal` cannot judge, `list_features` still prints a definite `facing` and `normal` for each face. These are the sign-canonical plane normal, so a bottom face reads `"facing": "up"`. Opposite walls share one normal. Nothing in the row says the outside was not known.

`lay_part_on_face` on the same face refuses, naming the reason:

```
list_features:    face:0x38c06ba55fa364b3  "facing": "up", "normal": [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]   bounds z 0.0 .. 0.0  (the bottom)
lay_part_on_face: face 0x38c06ba55fa364b3 of 'plate' belongs to an open body (its shell has holes), so its outside cannot be told - repair the mesh (fill its holes) or align to a closed part
```

This is the case #884 and #956 named: an agent picks faces by `facing` and `normal` for `locate_part`, `set_wcs_from_features` and operation geometry.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

The part is a 60 × 40 × 10 plate (z 0 to 10) with a 30 × 20 pocket, 5 deep, written as ASCII STL with outward winding (28 facets). Its top face is written as four rectangles around the pocket opening, so their long edges meet the pocket's top edges in T-junctions. Every facet is wound outward. For example, the bottom face's facets have normal −Z.

```json
[["import_model", {"path": "plate.stl"}],
 ["list_features", {"model": "plate"}],
 ["add_setup", {}],
 ["lay_part_on_face", {"face": {"model": "plate", "id": "face:0x38c06ba55fa364b3"}}]]
```

`list_features` faces, as printed:

| Face (bounds) | `facing` | `normal` |
|---|---|---|
| bottom, z 0 | `up` | `[0, 0, 1]` |
| wall y = −20 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| wall y = +20 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| wall x = −30 | `side` | `[1, 0, 0]` |
| wall x = +30 | `side` | `[1, 0, 0]` |
| pocket wall y = −10 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| pocket wall y = +10 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |

`lay_part_on_face` refuses as quoted above.

## Neighbour case that works

The same plate with its top ring written as four trapezoids, so every edge is shared by exactly two facets, is a closed shell. `list_features` gives the bottom `"down"` `[0, 0, -1]`, the walls their outward normals (`[0, -1, 0]` / `[0, 1, 0]`, `[-1, 0, 0]` / `[1, 0, 0]`), and the pocket walls pointing into the pocket. `lay_part_on_face` on its bottom succeeds ("Flip over X", outside −Z).

## Root cause (confirmed)

`outward()` in `crates/app/src/mcp/features.rs` calls `outward_normal` and, when it refuses, falls back to `world_dir(loc, fa.normal)`, the canonical normal. Its comment: "Where it refuses (an open or inside-out shell, no usable plane) the row keeps the canonical normal, placed - a listing must not fail on one face". `facing()` then makes "up" / "down" / "side" from whichever normal it got.

#956's "Done means" asked for the outward normal "or a refusal-shaped field when the winding is not decidable". The shipped fix (PR #1046) took the first half only.

The `camcraft-mcp` skill still carries #937's caveat in the `set_wcs_from_features` row: "a `list_features` face row's `normal` is the plane's canonical normal, not its outward side - tell faces apart by `bounds`". #956 asked for that note to be removed. As it stands, it is wrong for closed shells and is the only warning for open ones.

## Expected

The listing must not fail on one face, and it must not guess either. A face whose outside cannot be told says so in its row: for example, `facing` and `normal` null, or a flag with `outward_normal`'s reason. The skill note then describes that field instead of the old caveat.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a misleading field on the agent surface. The tools that act on a face refuse correctly.
- `effort:medium`: one module plus the skill row.
- `area:mcp`
- `source:agent`
